title: Self-supervised learning
reading: The slide introduces self-supervised learning as using the data itself as supervision, listing example pretext tasks: predicting oneself, predicting image rotation, and solving a jigsaw puzzle, among others. It then states the goals: learning representations from large-scale unlabeled data and learning high-level semantic representations. An accompanying image strip illustrates a jigsaw-style pretext task.

visuals.description: Three panels of a tiger photo: the original with a green 3x3 grid of patches overlaid, then the extracted 3x3 patch grid, then a shuffled/permuted version of the patches.
visuals.assertion: A jigsaw pretext task is created by cropping an image into a grid of patches and shuffling them, with the correct permutation acting as free supervision.

concepts.why_it_matters: Concrete surrogate objectives that generate supervision from data.
